Commentary.Commentary: Did the rain break hurt the Proteas? Perhaps. They struggled to grip the ball considering that it was wet and the bowling was not quite up to the mark. Well, for now, they have an irritating ask - to negotiate the dying moments before Stumps. Can they avoid any damage? The second innings is about to resume soon...

Hard day for the South Africans in the end. They started off erratically, only to be brought back by Kagiso Rabada and Tabraiz Shamsi. The duo bowled their hearts out, sharing 7 wickets between themselves but were not quite able to finish the job.

What a knock from Dimuth Karunaratne. The fourth Sri Lankan batsman to carry his bat through a completed innings. He judged the pitch to perfection and more importantly, did not throw it away. His innings was studded with 14 hits to the fence, of which one sailed over.

After electing to bat, Sri Lanka did not quite make use of the conditions. There was nothing much on the pitch except a bit of turn and some bounce but the batsmen just kept losing their wickets. Dimuth Karunaratne was the only man fighting hard and had it not been for the strong hands from Lakmal and Sandakan, the Lankans might have well folded up under 200.

What a batting display. Miserable till Tea. Then amazing after Tea. The first 8 wickets added 176 while the last 2 have accumulated 111. Boy o boy, the rain break has worked wonders for the home side.

OUT! Finally Sri Lanka have been bowled out. Shamsi does a repeat of what he did to Karunaratne a couple of balls ago. Sandakan jumps down the track, Shamsi throws it wide, the batsman has to reach out but misses. Easy stumping for QdK this time. SRI LANKA HAVE MANAGED 287.
On middle and leg, flicked towards square leg for a single.

SAFE. The keeper is indeed a little slow in knocking the bails off. Shamsi throws it miles outside off and Karunaratne, after coming down the track, sensing that he is beaten in flight, lets it go. He then tries to get back in his crease. De Kock collects, has to reach out for the ball and then whip the bails. It is referred upstairs and replays show that Karunaratne plonked his bat in but still managed to beat de Kock by a fraction of a second.
Stumped? In? One more decision goes to the third umpire. Karunaratne is the batsman.
Full and outside off, Karunaratne backs away and lofts it inside out over cover for a couple.
Outside off, left alone.
A short ball outside off, Lakshan initially looks to cut initially but then lets it go.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
FOUR! A long hop, Sandakan backs away and heaves it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Short and outside off, cut away through the covers for a single.
Outside off, Karunaratne gets down and reverse sweeps it through backward point. Calls for two and gets them.
Dean Elgar is asked to bowl now. Can he get that elusive wicket?
Full and around middle, Dimuth tries the paddle but gets a top edge which goes over the keeper, eluding Hashim Amla from first slip. A single taken.
Full and outside off, Lakshan swings it towards long on but the ball does not carry. Just a single.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.
Comes down the track again and hits it straight but finds silly mid on.
Mid on drops back while mid-wicket comes in...

FOUR! CRASH! That is some way to bring up the FIRST 50-RUN STAND OF THE INNINGS! Full and outside off, Sandakan puts on his dancing shoes, gets to the pitch of the ball and clobbers it down the ground past mid off for a boundary! Moves to 20 from 47 balls. What a crucial knock.
Full and outside off, Karunaratne backs away and lofts it over cover for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a couple. This is now the HIGHEST 10TH WICKET STAND FOR SRI LANKA VS SOUTH AFRICA in Tests.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
NO BALL. Maharaj oversteps now, bowls it outside off, Sandakan drives it towards cover.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Well, if you are wondering why did the players have that extra Drinks Break, it is because the scheduled close of play is 1758 local. Plenty of time left.
The batsman plays the slog sweep. They pick up a single.

150 UP FOR KARUNARATNE! At a stage when the Lankans were struggling to get to 200, this man has scored a 150 of his own. And rightly so, he has scored nearly 60 percent of the runs. Gets to the landmark by a gentle push towards mid off for a single.
This is dropped short now, Sandakan goes back and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Full and around off, Sandakan looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
Full and outside off, Dimuth lofts it over cover and gets a single. The stand is worth 40 now.
FOUR! CRACK! 2 short of a 150 now. A short ball, on middle, Karunaratne pulls it over mid-wicket and gets a boundary!
Flighted and full on off, blocked off the front foot to end the over.
Quicker and flatter on middle, Sandakan tries to flick but gets a leading edge wide of the point fielder.
Lunges to defend but it spins away to beat the outside edge.
Moves his weight on the back leg and slaps a short ball through point for a couple. Showing more confidence now.
Leans forward and defends it with the spin to the off side.
Goes on the back foot and works it in front of square leg for a single.
DRINKS BREAK...
Ball hits the batsman low on the pads.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
Full and outside off, Lakshan leans and drives it through the covers for a couple.
Full and outside off, very solid in defense is Sandakan.

FOUR! Well, he is going for it now. Full and outside off, Sandakan gets down and slogs it over mid-wicket. There is a man in the deep, Dale Steyn, but he cannot get to the ball. The stand is worth 30 now!!!
Full and around off, driven through mid off for a run.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Outside off, Sandakan lunges to defend but misses.
A full ball on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
Full and around off, blocked towards mid on.
Change of angle now... coming around the wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Down the leg side, Lakshan misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Full and outside off, Sandakan leans and plays a crisp-looking drive towards mid off.

Bizarre from Karunaratne. First, he pushes the ball towards point and declines what would have been an easy single. Then, when Dean Elgar returns a wild throw at the non-striker's end which is not backed up, he takes the single.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Short and outside fof, spinning away, Sandakan looks to cut but is beaten by the turn.
This time he leans and flicks it through square leg for a single. Strange. Moves to 140.
Full again, flicked through mid-wicket. Dimuth starts to run but then changes his mind.
Full and outside off, Karunaratne looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. An LBW appeal ensues but dies down pretty quickly. Impact was outside off.
Keshav Maharaj to bowl as well.
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Down the leg side, spinning away, left alone.
Tabraiz Shamsi is back on. South Africa would be worried now...

FOUR! Off the top edge but South Africa will not mind. They wanted Sandakan on strike and they have that now. A short ball, around leg, Karunaratne swivels to pull but gets a top edge which sails over the keeper to the fence behind. The stand is now worth 22.
Full and outside off, Karunaratne pushes it wide of mid off, sets off for a single but then changes his mind. Probably he should have taken that.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
A short ball, pulled towards mid-wicket.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket.

Some cramp issues now for Karunaratne. He is resting on the ground while the physio tends to him. To be honest, South Africa will not mind it too much. Around 45 minutes left for the close of play and neither of Markram or Elgar would be keen to bat now.
Comes down the track, Kagiso bowls it full and wide, DK has to reach out and manages to get it through cover for a run.
A short ball again, pulled towards long leg. No run taken.
Backs away down the leg side, Rabada follows him, bowls it short and Dimuth has to duck to avoid getting hurt. Falls on his back side.
Full and on middle, watchfully defended towards cover.
Another short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a couple this time.
A short ball again, pulled cleanly but straight to mid-wicket. No single taken again.
NO BALL. Steyn oversteps and bowls a short ball, Karunaratne pulls it through square leg. Does not take the single.
Now he arches back and deftly upper cuts it over the vacant second slip to third man for a single. Moves to 130.

FOUR! My word, this man can play in this gear as well? News to me. I thought he only participated in blockathons. Comes down the track, stays leg side of the ball, takes it on the half volley and crashes it through the covers for a boundary! The stand is worth 11 now.
A bouncer on middle, Sandakan ducks.
On middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
On middle and off, a touch short, punched towards cover.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
WIDE. A wayward bouncer, outside off, left alone.
A yorker on middle, well dug out.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.

'I think after taking the catch, he has rolled the ball onto the grass' are the words of the third umpire. In plain words, DROPPED. Sensational effort though. A short ball outside off, Karunaratne jumps down the track and slaps it over point. The fielder comes charging in, takes the catch (as per my view) but is not too sure. The two umpires then have a chat with one another and refer it to the third umpire, signalling it out. Nigel has a longggggggggggggggggggggggg look and eventually, rules it in favour of the batsman. Also, an interesting thing happens. The batsmen take two runs but the umpires are quick to spot that the second run was taken after the catch was completed - hence it becomes a dead ball after that. So just a single. Sandakan will face.

Has he taken that? The soft signal is out. The fielder is Dean Elgar. The bowler is Kagiso Rabada. The third umpire is Nigel Llong. Seems to be a decent catch, but then I am not the umpire or a judge to give a verdict.
A short ball around off, Karunaratne and swivels and looks to pull but gets a bottom edge through square leg.
Full and down the leg side, clipped through square leg for a couple.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, eased through point for a run.
Outside off, a play and a miss from Dimuth.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, Karunaratne comes down the track and slashes hard but misses.
Dale Steyn is back on.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it. 3 runs and a wicket from the over.
Full and outside off, Sandakan pushes at it with an open-bat face and goes behind point. Two runs taken.
Lakshan Sandakan is the last man in. Can he hang around with Karunaratne to take the total to 250?

OUT! That is a nasty delivery. A short ball, on middle and leg, Lakmal looks to tuck but the ball goes off his gloves and lobs straight up in the air. The Lankan skipper has no idea where the ball is but the people beside him have good idea. Quinton de Kock comes forward and takes the catch. Someone must have appealed because the umpire's finger went up. All I could see was only celebration. The 5-fer for Rabada still on. A useful stand of 48 has been broken.
A bouncer now, on middle and off, Lakmal ducks.
Outside off, pushed through point for a single.
A short ball, outside leg, Karunaratne looks to hook but the ball sails over the top edge.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

FOUR BYES! Useful runs. Down the leg side, Lakmal misses his flick, the keeper behind is blinded and the ball beats both and races to the fine leg fence. This is now the highest partnership in the innings. Worth 47.
A full toss, outside leg, flicked straight to square leg.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! A rare misjudgement from Dimuth. He looks to take on this short ball but plays it a bit early. Gets a top edge which goes high up in the air. Keshav Maharaj comes running across to his left from deep square leg, puts in a slide but the ball lands short. Two runs taken.
Excellent yorker on middle and off, Karunaratne digs it out towards cover.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Down the leg side, Lakmal misses his flick and a leg bye is stolen.
A short ball, on middle, pulled beautifully through mid-wicket for a single.
Full again, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full again, driven straight to mid off.
Tossed up on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Advances down to the pitch of the delivery and knocks it down to long on for a run.
Flighted and full on off, driven back to the bowler.
DRINKS BREAK.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Stays back to punch it through the line. Attempts for the single and dives in an ugly manner to reach the other end. The fielder also had a shy at the bowler's end but failed to find the target.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
A short ball, around off, angling away, Karunaratne pulls but mistimes it to short mid-wicket.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Kagiso Rabada is back on. 9-1-35-3 so far. Shamsi was tiring...
Comes down a track a touch and pushes it towards mid on.
Almost through! Full and outside off, SL comes forward to defend but his bat hits his pad and the ball spins past the outside edge.
Stays back and punches it towards cover.
Plenty of turn. Maharaj gives this a lot of loop and revolutions on this one, lands it outside off, Suranga stays back to defend but the ball spins past the outside edge.
Fuller, around off, watchfully defended.
Quicker one outside off, a touch short, Lakmal looks to cut but misses.
Gets down, takes the ball on the full and gently paddles it through fine leg for a couple.
Dragged short, on middle, heaved towards deep mid-wicket for a run.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
Tossed up on middle, Suranga looks to defend but misses and is hit on the pads.
Full and outside off, Lakmal drives it straight down the ground. Keshav Maharaj gets across from mid off, slides but a year too early. Two runs taken.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Tossed up around off, Lakmal gets a good stride and defends.
The darter on middle, Lakmal looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
The batsman has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Works it through mid-wicket for a brace again.
Outside off, Karunaratne reverse sweeps it behind point for a couple.
Keshav Maharaj is back on... after a long time.
Full toss outside off, bashed towards mid off.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries. A tad short, around off, spinning in, Karunaratne just helps it through square leg.

FOUR! 8th century for Karunaratne in Tests, his 4th 50-plus score in his last 5 innings batting first! Nice way to get it too. Comes down the track, takes the ball on the full and drives it straight down the ground for a boundary! The dressing room is standing tall and applauding. The two batsmen in the middle hug each other. Reason to smile, yes. But now, the Lankans need to think about getting some sort of a decent first innings score.
On middle, played straight to short mid-wicket.

THREE BYES. Forget the runs. Karunaratne is back on strike. Full and down the leg side, Lakmal looks to flick but misses. The ball spins from the rough, goes past the batsman and the keeper, eludes a lazy effort from Dean Elgar at leg slip but still does not reach the ropes. Three runs taken.
Around off, solidly defended. Not throwing it away...
CLOSE!!! Very straight, on middle and off, Dimuth looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. Could have so easily rolled onto the stumps.
Okay... 99 time...
Outside off, played through point for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked.
Outside off, coming in a long way, Lakmal looks to flick but misses. The ball beats the inside edge and just shaves the off stump!
Full on middle, driven straight down the ground for a single. Moves to 99...
FOUR! Glorious shot! A full ball outside off, Lakmal leans and drives it wide of mid off for a boundary!
Full and around off, Suranga looks to drive but gets a thick inside edge onto his left boot.
Tossed up generously around leg stump, Lakmal plays all around it as he looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
Moves to 98... pushes it towards mid on for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Outside off, played through point for a couple.
Comes down the track and has a hack. The ball goes off the inside edge and goes towards fine leg. A single taken.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a run.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and around off, defended watchfully.
Ball hits the batsman low on the pads. A strong appeal from the bowler and fielders. The umpire shows no interest in the appeal.
Full toss outside off, driven straight to mid off.

Pitched on middle, Lakmal looked to defend but missed and was hit on the pads. Shamsi appealed but the umpire shook his head. The bowler and captain had a chat and perhaps there was a chat regarding the inside edge. Oh dear... replays do not detect any inside edge and Hawk Eye says that the BALL WILL HIT THE LEG STUMP!
The captain is out to the middle now - Suranga Lakmal.

OUT! Gone by more than a yard. Poor Herath. Dimuth came down the track and whipped it wide of mid on. The striker had come halfway down the track for the single. Herath meanwhile, was ball watching and started to run after he saw Dimuth halfway down. Now Karunaratne stopped but then continued to run. Herath started his locomotor but after Philander got to the ball. All the fielder had to do was pick up and throw to the keeper who did the rest. Herath put in a dive and then started to walk back. He was almost near the boundary ropes by the time the decision was given.
Is that gone? De Kock seems confident. Herath seems to be in despair. Third umpire will give the decision on the status of the pair...
Comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.

FOUR! CLOUT! Very rarely does one use such words for Karunaratne. But he seems to have realized that the scoreboard is not moving and someone has got to do something about it - better be the set man. Full and on off, Dimuth gets down and mows it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Three in a row. Vernon continues to probe around off, DK looked to defend but the ball straightened a touch and went off the inside edge through square leg. A run taken.

That looked stone dead. Only for some wood. This was pretty straight, Dimuth looked to flick this one but missed. Was hit flush on the pads and Philander started to go up in an appeal but then spotted the inside edge.
Full and straight, Karunaratne looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Walks a couple of steps towards the pacer and then shoulders arms.
A tad short, on middle, Herath swivels and pulls it through square leg for a single. Gets off the mark.
A touch short, pulled through mid-wicket for a brace again.

South Africa are spending extra time trying to dry the ball. The outfield has been ruled dry enough for play to carry on but clearly there is plenty of water on the field as can be seen from the Proteas' reaction...
Full and down the leg side, swept fine for a couple.
Very full, around off, watchfully blocked.
Better shot. Waits for the ball to come, it is pretty much similar to the previous one and this time he gets it past backward point for a couple.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
One more leave outside off.
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, pretty wide, left alone.
Rangana Herath is the new man in at number 9, replacing Dilruwan.

OUT! My word - what was that from de Kock? Almost like a net session! But nothing sort of a warm-up from Philander. He comes running in, bowls it right on the money, around off, on a length and then makes it to move away a touch. Dilruwan pushes at it and gets a healthy outside edge. The ball flies right into the gloves of de Kock who just takes it with one hand! Seems surprised and so are we. So why do you need spin from both ends? Not if wickets are falling in quick succession... 250TH INTERNATIONAL WICKET FOR PHILANDER.
Vernon Philander is back on to bowl. One would have thought we might see spin from both ends for more time...
A touch short and around off, Karunaratne moves back and hits it against the spin through mid-wicket for a brace. End of a successful over.
Eases a full ball down to long on and crosses for a single.
Shortish and on middle, turning down, Perera fails to put bat on ball and gets hit on the thigh pad.

MISSING LEG! Too much turn has saved Dilruwan. We all got tricked there. A loopy full ball landing just outside off and spinning back in to beat the forward defensive prod of Perera. It strikes him on the pads, they appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Dilruwan opts for the DRS and it finds the ball to be missing leg.
Shout for an lbw! Up goes the finger and Perera has reviewed it. Looks out. Let's see...

That was quick! The groundsmen have done a wonderful job in mopping up all the water on the covers. We are all set to get underway again. Dilruwan Perera has joined Dimuth Karunaratne in the middle. Tabraiz Shamsi to complete his over.

Update 1442 local - We're back. No rain we are hearing which is superb news. But the covers are still on and we can see some water on it. Won't be a prompt start, sadly. Stay with us for more updates.
...DAY 1, THIRD SESSION...

Outstanding session for the touring team. It was a mixed-bag play in the morning where the honours were shared. Things completely changed though after the Lunch break. The South African bowlers found their rhythm and snapped three wickets in the first hour. Kagiso Rabada once again was in his elements and bowled with a lot of venom, resulting in the wickets of Mathews and Roshen. Tabraiz Shamsi bowled relentlessly from one end and was very impressive. Given the nature of the pitch, the Lankans would be hoping that they somehow get to 250, if not more, but for that to happen, someone needs to give company to Karunaratne who is going strong and is 20 shy of a century. An exciting evening session awaits us, provided the rain stays away. Do join us in a short while.

We are getting the confirmation that early TEA has been taken. The conditions though have brightened up in the middle. Having said that, some dark and angry looking clouds are still lurking around. Let's keep our fingers crossed for a prompt start after the break.

With that wicket, the heavens have opened up. The players are rushing off the field as it's raining heavily all of a sudden. The groundsmen charge in to the centre with the covers and in no time, they have covered the playing area. Will we have any more play in this session? Stay with us to find out.

OUT! This was always on the cards with the ball spinning away from the southpaw. Shamsi tosses it up nicely and lands it full around off. Dickwella gets half-forward to defend but it turns away to catch the outside edge. Amla makes no mistake at first slip and the 42-run association has been broken. Brilliant bowling by the chinaman, he has been on song with his line and length, which is so unlike a wrist spinner. For Niroshan, it's a case of yet another start not getting converted. Must be frustrating for him. Also, did the movement near the boundary line by the groundsmen put him off? We hardly see him offering a straight bat in defense and he could have played this ball differently had there been no threat of approaching rain. These are all assumptions though.
Turning away from the batsman but the length is on the shorter side. Dickwella rocks back and slaps it through cover-point for a couple of runs.
Flatter and shorter on off, it's been punched off the back foot to mid-wicket. No run to end the over.
Goes down on one knee and sweeps it with the spin to long leg for a run.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Walks down to the pitch of the delivery and pushes it back to the bowler.

Dickwella tries to be innovative. Receives a low full toss on off and he brings out the reverse sweep. Doesn't come from the middle of the bat but it still has enough to speed past Amla at first slip. By the time it has been retrieved in the deep, they take a couple of runs.
Flighted and full outside off, driven off the front foot to the cover fielder.
Floated full on off, turning away, Dimuth tries to flick but gets a leading edge towards point.
Very full and on off, driven down the ground to mid off.
Turning square off the pitch. Karunaratne gets back to defend but is beaten.
The groundsmen are making a move. It has turned gloomy now and maybe they are expecting some rain. Let's hope there is no interruption.
Floated around off, it's been swept in front of square leg for a run.
Sharp spin away from the batsman, Dickwella pushes at it and misses.
Flighted and full on middle, Dickwella stays back when he should have been forward and defends it off the outer half of the bat to covers.
And again. The length continues to be very full from Keshav and it's getting easily driven. Karunaratne finds the gap at covers and picks yet another couple of runs in this over.
Gives this one some extra air and lands it full outside off. Karunaratne drives it through covers and returns for the second run.
Advances down the track to a full ball and pushes it out towards the cover fielder.
Nicely played. Tossed up and around off, Karunaratne paddles it down to fine leg for a couple. 150 up for Sri Lanka!
Flighted and full on off, it's knocked down to long on for a run.
Flatter full ball on off, Dickwella defends it with firm hands towards the bowler.
Keshav Maharaj is into the attack now, replacing Rabada.
Well flighted and full on middle, hit across the line but straight to the mid-wicket fielder.
Tossed up ball on off, defended near the front pad by Dimuth.
This time Shamsi fails to land his delivery. Karunaratne gets down on one knee and sweeps the full toss to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Superbly bowled. Turning away from the batsman outside off, Dimuth lunges to defend but is beaten.
Extra flight but the length is too full on middle. It's been driven back to the bowler.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it with the spin to the off side.
A length ball angling away from the batsman, Karunaratne taps it off his back foot towards the vacant space in the cover region. A single to end the over. Rabada seems to be tiring now.
Bouncer around leg, Dimuth ducks underneath it.
Straighter in line and this time it has been flicked nicely through square leg. A couple of runs taken.
Pitches it full and on middle, Karunaratne falls over a bit on the off side as he flicks this one. Connection ain't entirely from the middle of the bat as it goes straight to mid-wicket.

Once again it's shortish in length around middle, Dickwella stays back inside the crease to present a straight bat in defense. It gathers the inside half of the bat and speeds through square leg for a run.
Back of a length ball on middle, defended off the back foot by Niroshan.
Play and a miss! Shamsi delivers it short around off, seeing that, Karunaratne rocks back and attempts to pull. However, the ball spins away to beat his bat. Tabraiz smiles.
Flighted on off, defended off the front foot.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Fails to read the variation, Dimuth. A wrong 'un, landing on middle, Karunaratne is inside the crease, completely clueless as he misses the ball and is hit on the pads. They appeal but it's missing leg.
Floated full ball on off, defended watchfully off the front foot by Karunaratne.
Flatter, shorter and wider outside off. Spinning away. Dickwella delays his shot a bit and dabs it past backward point for a single.
Short and wide outside off, DK cuts it off his back foot but finds the point fielder.
Back of a length delivery on off, Karunaratne stands back inside the crease and whacks it through covers for a couple. Looks a lot assured while staying back and playing his shots, Dimuth.
A wild delivery. Way wide outside off, left alone by the batsman and the umpire called it a wide. First extra of this innings.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Short and on middle, pulled down to fine leg where Shamsi made a tumbling stop. A couple taken again.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. Two runs added to the total.
Good length ball outside off, Karunaratne punches it off his back foot to covers.
Too full and on leg, swept behind square leg for a couple of runs.
Peach of a delivery. Drifting into the batsman around off, Dickwella once again is beaten as he tries to defend but the ball spins away from his willow.

Nothing but daylight. Waste of a review. Faf really should be unimpressed with his keeper. A delivery spinning away from the batsman, Dickwella tries to defend off his front foot but misses. It spins and bounces past his bat, de Kock collects it and jumps in joy. The bowler also joins him in appealing but the umpire refuses. Du Plessis opts for the DRS after listening to Quinton but only disappointment came after that for South Africa.
Shout for a caught behind. Not given. Quinton de Kock though is very sure and convinces his skipper to go for the DRS. The way they are celebrating, it seems there was an outside edge. Let's see...
Uppish but safe. Turning into the batsman, from a fuller length, Dickwella flicks it across the line but not with much conviction. It loops in the air but doesn't carry to mid on.

Flighted and full on off, driven through covers. Karunaratne set off for a run but his partner is ball-watching. So, he also decides to watch the ball as de Kock screams Temba! Temba! But before anything else happens, Dickwella rushes across, responds to the call and makes it safely to the other end.

In the air... safe! Dickwella is living dangerously. A flighted full ball just outside off, spinning away, Niroshan tries to sweep it across the line but gets a top edge. It flies over the keeper and past the outstretched right hand of Hashim Amla (first slip). Runs behind and they take three runs.

Drinks break. A fine hour post Lunch for South Africa. They have picked three wickets in quick time and are on top. Cannot afford to relax though as every run scored on this pitch will be crucial. Needless to say, Sri Lanka need someone to stick around with Karunaratne. Let's see what the next hour has in store for us.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Rabada errs in his line and slips a full ball down the leg side, Karunaratne neatly deflects it off his pads to the fine leg fence.
Rabada is in excellent rhythm at the moment. Bangs in yet another bouncer, nicely directed, Dimuth ducks.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They've managed to run three.
Back of a length delivery on middle, defended off the back foot.

Boom on the helmet. Rabada is mixing his length quite well. Digs it in short, well-directed, Niroshan takes his eyes off the ball as he tries to get away from the line. Takes a blow on his helmet this time. A very uneasy stay in the middle for the Lankan wicketkeeper.

Not out! It's indeed pitching outside leg. A sharp delivery, speared in, Dickwella is stuck inside the crease, his feet went nowhere as he tried to flick. Got beaten for pace, missed the ball completely to get hit on the pads. Looked dead to the naked eye and the finger went up after the appeal. Dickwella took the DRS and the replays showed it to be landing outside leg. A reprieve to ND all thanks to the technology.
Huge shout for an lbw and up goes the finger. The South Africans are celebrating but Dickwella wants it to get reviewed. Pitching outside leg?
Flighted full ball on off, turning in, Karunaratne leans forward and defends it off the inner half of the bat.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Flighted and outside off, going straight on, Dickwella goes down to slog sweep but misses.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

What happened there? Tossed up ball on off, turning in with some extra bounce, Dickwella tries to sweep but misses. It hits his gloves and deflects onto his helmet. The extra protection behind the helmet comes off on the impact. The ball rolls towards Markram at short leg who has an immediate shy at the striker's end. No harm done.
Short and wide outside off, punched to sweeper cover for a single.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. End of a superlative over by KG, a double-wicket maiden!
Another back foot defense by Dickwella.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Niroshan Dickwella arrives in the middle.

OUT! Rabada is a special, special bowler. An effort delivery by him. He bends his back and lets out a roaring rising delivery around off. Roshen has never seen the ball jumping on so much in Sri Lanka. He is caught in an awkward position as he goes on his toes to fend at it. The ball takes the splice of his bat and loops towards short leg. Markram is alert there and stretches low to his right to take the catch safely. Rabada smiles, third scalp for him.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Roshen Silva is the new batsman. Dark clouds are also approaching the stadium.

OUT! An inspirational bowling change by Faf du Plessis and Kagiso Rabada has nipped out Angelo Mathews. He bowls it on a length around off, Angelo is stuck inside the crease as he tries playing at it with an angled bat as the ball moves away. Very unsure from the former Lankan skipper as he nicks it behind for Quinton de Kock. A very simple catch for the Protea keeper and Rabada has two.
Kagiso Rabada is back on.
Fullish on off, driven down the ground to mid off. Just the second maiden of this innings.
Karunaratne has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and landing on leg, turning towards off after that as Karunaratne attempts to flick. He closes the face of the bat early and it pops out off the leading edge. Doesn't carry to anyone.
Tossed up ball landing full outside off, Karunaratne leans to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

Dropped! Never easy at short leg. These kind of chances stick or they don't. Flighted and full ball on middle, it's flicked across the line and is uppish. Markram tries to catch it but it hits his body and dies down before he could react.
Short and outside off, cut from the back foot but straight to the cover-point fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A length ball on off, angling in, Mathews remains inside the crease as he defends it back to the bowler.
Lands it full and outside off, some extra bounce, Karunaratne presses forward and drives it on the up towards the cover region. A single taken.
Short again, on middle, Mathews eases it down to long leg and crosses.
A touch short and on off, this time Mathews taps it down comfortably towards short leg. On one bounce to Markram it goes.
Bangs in a shortish ball on middle, Mathews takes his eyes off the ball and somehow keeps it out on the leg side.
Flighted and full on middle, driven with the spin but straight to the cover fielder.
Loopy and on middle, Karunaratne is solid in his front foot defense.
Nicely flighted this time. Full and on off, spinning a bit away, Dimuth defends it off his front foot.
Very full and on middle, driven down the ground past the bowler to mid off.
Once again the line is too straight and it has been worked fine down the leg side for a couple of runs.
Tossed up ball on middle, flicked on the leg side but straight to the fielder.
On a shortish length around off, Mathews defends it off his back foot to the off side.
A length ball on off, Mathews defends it off his back foot to the leg side.
Mathews lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Greets the new batsman with a well-cooked bouncer. Mathews ducks.
In walks Angelo Mathews.

OUT! Soft dismissal! Steyn strikes and roars in delight. He delivers it on a fuller length around middle, maybe it sticks a bit on the pitch as Mendis is early into the flick shot. Ends up chipping a straightforward catch to Kagiso Rabada at mid on. A nothing shot in the end and it brings the curtains down on Kusal's knock. So, this is the second wicket falling more due to the assistance from the pitch than anything else. Such deliveries usually get whipped through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Good length delivery around off, it's punched off the back foot and the ball rolls through point for a couple of runs.
Loopy and drifting in around off, Karunaratne strides forward and defends it near his front pad.
Another flick shot by Mendis and this time he finds the gap at mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted and full on off, defended off the front foot.
Nicely tossed up again, full and on middle, it's flicked past short leg. Finds backward square leg.
Floated full ball on off, spinning back in, Mendis lunges and defends it off the inner half of the bat to mid-wicket.
Turning down the leg side, Kusal tries to flick but misses. The line has been quite inaccurate from Shamsi.
FOUR! Fine, fine shot! A fractionally short of a length delivery outside off, angling away, Karunaratne stands tall inside the crease and pulls it powerfully through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Spears it very full on middle, Karunaratne keeps it out safely at mid on.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Zippy delivery, leaving the batsman outside off, Mendis has a poke at it but misses.

15th Test fifty fir Dimuth Karunaratne! Full and around off, angling away, Dimuth plays a punch drive through covers and takes a single. Good knock so far by him. He raises his bat to acknowledge the applause from his teammates.
Fullish and on off, driven back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Is that a catch? Nopes, it isn't. For a moment, the on-air commentators got excited. Flatter full ball on off, Mendis tries to drive but it spins back in to take the inside edge. On one bounce it goes to Markram at short leg but de Kock ain't aware of it and shouts catch itttt. Aiden shows no excitement at short leg though.
Flighted and full outside off, Mendis drives it back towards the bowler.
A loopy full ball landing on leg and spinning down, Mendis tries to flick but misses. Another good take by de Kock.
Tossed up ball on off, turning in, it's defended off the back foot.
Short and spinning away after landing outside off, Karunaratne slaps it to sweeper cover for one.
Short and on middle, pulled in front of square leg for one.

FOUR! Off the gloves, beating the despairing dive from Quinton de Kock. A well-directed short ball by Steyn, Karunaratne tries to pull but it takes his gloves and flies past the diving keeper to the fine leg fence. Dimuth seems to have hurt his fingers but is ready to face the next ball. Maybe, will ask for physio after the over ends.
Digs in a bouncer around leg, Dimuth ducks underneath it.
FOUR! Serves it full and outside off, Karunaratne pushes at it with firm hands and places it through the gap between gully and backward point for a boundary.
Lands it on a length around off, shaping back in a bit, Mendis softly works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Back of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot to mid-wicket.
Interesting. South Africa have decided to bowl pace from one end. Dale Steyn it is. A couple of slips in place.
A bit flatter through the air, full and on middle, spinning away, DK defends it by getting forward. Not quite from the middle of the bat.
Extra flight this time as it lands very full on off. Dimuth drives it back to the bowler.
Full again, around off, Karunaratne lunges and defends it back.
Turning away from the batsman after landing full outside off. Dimuth picks it well and lets it through to the keeper.
Tossed up ball on middle, Karunaratne defends it off his front foot.

Starts the session with a short delivery outside off, Karunaratne rocks back and cuts it with the turn to deep point. It slows down before the rope as the sweeper cover fielder picks it up and sends the throw to the keeper. A couple taken.

Welcome back for the afternoon session. The players march out to the middle. Once again a quick huddle for South Africa before they spread on the field. So, what to expect in this session from the Proteas? Spin, spin and some more spin. Starting with Tabraiz Shamsi. Here we go...
...DAY 1, SECOND SESSION...

There is plenty in the pitch for the spinners and expect Keshav Maharaj and Tabraiz Shamsi to dominate proceedings after the Lunch break. Dimuth Karunaratne has applied himself superbly and Sri Lanka will hope that he bats long. Kusal Mendis has looked a bit uneasy although he is striking at almost run-a-ball. South Africa will be worried already but they cannot afford to think too ahead. First thing first, their aim will be to restrict the home team to a low first innings total. Will they succeed? Do join us in a short while to find out.

Mixed session! Sri Lanka scored runs, 93 to be precise and South Africa picked up a couple of wickets. The hosts after electing to bat started well with their openers looking comfortable. Vernon Philander and Dale Steyn weren't accurate with their lines and conceded runs at a quick pace. It was Kagiso Rabada and his class which brought South Africa their first wicket. The second wicket was more due to the turn on offer from the pitch as Dhananjaya lost his stumps.

FOUR! Some starter before Lunch by Maharaj (In India a cook is called a maharaj)! Friendly full toss on off, Mendis kneels and nails his sweep shot through mid-wicket for a boundary. The umpire takes the bails off and the players are leaving the field. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Beauty! Drifting into the batsman and landing full around off, Mendis has to play at it but gets beaten due to the away spin.
Loopy and full around off, driven of the front foot towards silly mid off.
The length is on the shorter side outside off, it's cut off the back foot through point. Bavuma chases it down and the batsmen cross for a couple.
Steps down the track and knocks it down to long on for one.
Flighted and on off, driven through covers for a single.
Slight spin away from the batsman, Karunaratne stays back and punches it square of the wicket on the off side. Dot ball to end the over.
Karunaratne has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Turning down the leg side, Dimuth tries to flick but misses.
Tickles it off his pads through mid-wicket and crosses for a run.
That went too quickly to short leg. Mendis whips his flick shot across the line and it hits Markram flush on his left shin pad and rolls in the opposite direction. No time to react.
FOUR! Shamsi drags his length short and it's going down the leg side. Mendis gets back to pull and in spite of it staying low, he puts it away through backward square leg for a boundary.
Dale Steyn returns on the field.
Gets forward to defend and keeps it out from the inside half of the bat.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.
Goes down on one knee for the sweep shot but it takes the bottom half of the bat and rests on the surface.
Very full and on middle, flicked on the leg side but straight towards short leg. On one bounce.
Too full in length on middle, Mendis keeps it out towards short leg.
Loopy and on off, pushed with an angled bat towards point.
Heinrich Klaasen is on the field as Dale Steyn has gone back to the pavilion.
Quietly eases it down through mid on for a run.
Strides forward and drives it down to long off for one.
Flatter on off, blocked off the back foot.
A floated one on off, driven off the front foot to covers. Shamsi won't mind that shot with the ball turning square.
Plays with the spin on this occasion and pushes it out to covers.
Flighted and outside off, turning away, Karunaratne tries playing at it but is beaten by the away spin.
Flatter on off, defended off the back foot.

FOUR! Loopy delivery spinning down the leg side, Mendis gets down on one knee to play the sweep shot but fails to make proper connection. It beats de Kock behind the stumps and races away to the fine leg fence. The umpire signals it as runs and the replays pick a bit of Mendis' gloves. Hmm... not a convincing way to reach the milestone but still a big achievement. 2000 Test runs for Kusal!
Tossed up outside off, driven towards mid off for a run.
Very full on middle, eased behind square leg for a single.
Flighted and full on middle, Mendis wristily works it down to mid on.
Too full and on off, pushed down to long on for one.
Spinning back in from around off, Mendis goes inside the crease and keeps it out at the last moment.
Mendis has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Kusal Mendis is the number 4 batsman.

OUT! Through the gate! Shamsi is delighted and runs in joy. Brilliant delivery. Generously tossed up just outside off, landing on a fuller length, de Silva tries to drive it through covers but it spins back in big time, beats the inside part of the bat and hits the top of off stump. Dhananjaya has a surprised look on his face, smiles a bit before leaving the ground. So much turn on this delivery, alarming for South Africa also as Sri Lanka possess three quality spinners in their ranks. Add to that, the Proteas will be batting last on this deck.
Drives it with the spin down to deepish mid off for a run.
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it down.
Karunaratne has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Maharaj is a superb fielder off his own bowling. An off drive by Dhananjaya this time and Keshav flies to his left to stop the ball.
Hammers a full ball back towards the bowler who dives across to his right to stop the ball. Very well done.
Arm ball on off, skidding in, Dhananjaya keeps it out from the back foot.
Floated and full on middle, blocked off the front foot back towards the bowler.
Dances down the track to take it on the full but mishits it towards short leg. De Kock shouts catch it as he thought it went off the boot. Nothing such in the replays.
Change of ends for Keshav Maharaj.
Drops it short this time, on middle, Karunaratne pulls it to deep mid-wicket. Rabada rushes across to his right from fine leg and slides to stop the ball. A couple of runs taken.
Spinning away from the southpaw, Karunaratne tries to cut but misses.
Once again Dimuth plays it with the spin back towards the bowler.
Gets forward to  a full ball and drives it towards mid off.
Dimuth has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up ball outside off, spinning away, Karunaratne defends it off his back foot.
Tabraiz Shamsi into the attack. Interesting change, unless it's for swapping ends. Keshav got good purchase.
Outside off, left alone to end a fantastic over.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Bumper! A well-directed one. On a lifeless pitch. Rabada is a special bowler. Making a Galle pitch look like a Durban one. Extracts extra pace and bounce and catches de Silva in an awkward position. He shapes up for the pull shot initially but then tries to bail out. But by then it has taken his gloves and gone wide of short leg. Markram reacts to his left but fails to reach the chance in time. Dhananjaya survives a scare.

That would have hurt! Rabada bowls it short and Dhananjaya connects well with his pull shot but it hits Markram flush on the grille of his helmet at short leg. It then deflects onto his right shoulder before settling down near the pitch. Aiden not showing much pain though.
Stays back and punches it towards mid on for a run.
A length ball on off, defended from the crease.

Whoa! What was that? Spitting cobra. Maharaj gives this one some extra flight and lands it somewhere around middle. Dhananjaya thinks of playing at it from the crease but it shoots up to beat the bat. Nearly kissed the outside edge. Good take by de Kock. Rangana Herath will be licking his lips after watching that.
This one is very full on off, Dhananjaya keeps it out at the last moment.
Too full in length around off, Karunaratne steps down the track and digs it out through mid-wicket for a run. Nearly got deceived in flight.
This time the batsman finds the gap with his off drive and picks up a single. There is a fielder in the deep.
Once again Dhananjaya strokes it with the spin towards the bowler.
Gets forward and drives it with the spin on the off side.
Shortish and outside off, defended from the back foot to point.
Pitches it up and outside off, de Silva drives it down the ground and Shamsi chases it from mid off. Three taken.
Another delivery which is drifting down the leg side. Dhananjaya is beaten for pace on this occasion as he fails to connect with his flick shot. Takes a blow on his thigh pad.
Uneasy moment. Rabada angles a length ball on middle and leg, de Silva tries to flick but it takes the leading edge and rolls to point.
Identical length again but this one is bowled in the line of the off stump. De Silva defends it off his back foot.
Back of a length delivery in the channel outside off, Dhananjaya allows it through to the keeper.
Nicely tossed up delivery, a good loop as it lands full around off. Dhananjaya strides forward and pushes it softly towards backward point for a run.

This one is bowled a bit in the flatter trajectory. Fullish and down the leg side. De Silva tries to flick but misses and it goes off his left boot to the point region. For a moment, the close-in fielders got excited but there was no bat involved.
Loopy and full on off, defended watchfully off the front foot.
Dhananjaya has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Fine footwork by Dhananjaya. Gives himself room by staying leg side to this delivery and then dances down the track to loft it with the spin over extra cover. Catch it is the shout but it goes well wide of the mid off fielder. A boundary.
Flighted full ball on middle, driven back to the bowler.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Fuller and drifting down the leg side, Karunaratne fails to flick it off his pads.

FOUR! Streaky. Karunaratne had no idea how and where it went. Rabada angles in a good length ball around off, straightening a touch with extra bounce, Karunaratne stays back to defend but it takes the splice of his bat and hurries past the slip cordon for a boundary.
Digs in a bouncer, Karunaratne ducks.
Fractionally short and on off, defended off the back foot to the off side.

FOUR! Serves it on a back of a length outside off, Karunaratne stands tall and punches it square of the wicket on the off side. If it's chase from a fielder, it  has to be Maharaj today. Seems to have taken a contract for that. Although, this time the ball wins the race to the fence. The outfield is getting quickened up probably with the sun coming down. 50 comes up for Sri Lanka.
Change of ends for Kagiso Rabada. He will be bowling from around the wicket for the left-hander...
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot by Dhananjaya.
Charges down the track and knocks it down to long on for a run.

Shout for an lbw! Not given. Sharp spin from around off, from a fuller length, Karunaratne gets forward to defend but misses. He is hit on the pads, they appeal but the umpire shakes his head. No DRS taken. Faf probably feels that it's turning too much. The replays confirm the same. Would have spun down and clipping the leg stump at the most.
Presses forward to a full ball and drives it down to long off for a run.
Flighted and very full around off, driven off the front foot and Maharaj dived to his left to make the stop.
And here he comes... Keshav Maharaj to bowl!

Drinks break. A good first hour of this Test match. Runs came thick and fast earlier but then South African managed to pick the wicket of Karunaratne. They would have got Gunathilaka also had they used DRS in the first over. Nothing extravagant in the pitch for the pacers. Let's see if there is spin as and when South Africa bring Keshav Maharaj.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under it at the last moment.
Shortish and moving down the leg side, it's worked off the pads behind square leg for one.
Speedy delivery. Full and just outside off, Dhananjaya covers his stumps and shoulders arms.
Steyn delivers it on a full length around off, shaping in a bit, de Silva is caught inside the crease as he tries to defend. Gets a thick inside edge onto the pads.
Short and pulled on the leg side for a single.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
De Silva has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. End of a successful over for South Africa.

Appeal for a bat-pad! Nothing doing as far as Paul Reiffel is concerned. Good length ball on middle and angling down down. Dhananjaya tries to flick but seems to have missed. It goes off his thigh pad to short leg where Markram catches it and they appeal. Off the thigh pad and nothing off the bat, confirms the replay.
Dhananjaya de Silva is the number 3 batsman.

OUT! Gone! Doesn't matter if there is life or not in the pitch, Rabada will get something going for him. Such is his class. Serves a good length delivery outside off and extracts some extra bounce. Gunathilaka is back footed as he tries to punch it through the line. But the ball reaches high on his bat, kisses the outside edge and de Kock grabs it with ease. Rabada is ecstatic as he celebrates with his teammates. The umpire after raising his finger quickly checks for the front foot and the third umpire also checks for the edge. Wonder why? Anyway, everything is fine and legal as a disappointed Danushka returns to the pavilion.
Stands back to a shortish ball and defends it to the off side.

FOUR! Poor fielding at mid on. A fractionally short of a length delivery on off, Gunathilaka drags his pull shot from the front foot and it races off the inside half of the bat. Philander is lazy in putting a dive and does so after the ball has gone past him. A boundary results.
In the channel outside off, Gunathilaka watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
Once again it's shortish and just outside off, Karunaratne plays it out from the crease to mid off.
Back of a length delivery on middle and leg, Karunaratne gets on this toes and defends it to mid-wicket.
Another bouncer by Steyn, this one though is too high and hence Karunaratne ducks.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

SIX! Nearly fell to the plan though, Dimuth. Steyn digs in a short delivery with two fielders back in the deep on the leg side. Karunaratne still wheels a pull shot and gets good enough connection to clear the rope at backward square leg. South Africa won't mind that much, if he keeps playing his shots.
Play and a miss! A zippy delivery, landing on a fuller length and skidding away. Karunaratne gets forward to push at it but misses.
Some movement again for Rabada as he lands it on a length around middle and off. Danushka does well to play it with soft hands towards gully.
Lets out a fuller length ball on middle, it's pushed off the front foot to mid off.
Stays tall in his crease to a shortish ball and punches it past short extra cover for one.
Beaten! Delivers it with a scrambled seam but still it moves appreciably away from the batsman. Karunaratne has an area of vulnerability outside off as he pushes and misses.
Bowls this one on middle and off, on a good length again, Karunaratne defends it from the crease.
Starts with a good length ball outside off, Karunaratne allows it through.
Here comes the first bowling change. The number one Test bowler, Kagiso Rabada is unleashed into the attack. Two slips in place for him.
Good length ball around leg, worked off the pads to the leg side but straight to the fielder.
Bangs in a bouncer, around middle, Gunathilaka picks it early and sways away from the line.
Straighter in line, Dimuth eases it off his pads past the left side of the square leg umpire. A single taken.
A length delivery on middle and off, defended from the crease.
Outside off, left alone.
Serves it around off on a length, Karunaratne covers the line and defends it back.
Lands it on a length around off, moving away a shade, Gunathilaka pushes it with gentle hands through backward point and collects a couple of runs. It's a big over, 10 runs off it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Once again a confident front foot drive by Gunathilaka but he finds the mid off fielder. The pitch looks excellent for stroke-making with nothing much in it for the pacers.
Fuller in length and around off, defended off the front foot.

FOUR! This is very poor bowling from Philander. Not getting his line right. Bowls it wide outside off, on a length, Gunathilaka smashes it off his back foot through cover-point and this time the ball trickles past the rope.
FOUR! Eased away! Philander errs in line and bowls it a bit short around middle and leg. Gunathilaka stands back inside the crease and glances it off his hips to the fine leg fence.
Make it three leaves in a row to end the over.
Once again Karunaratne lets a length ball go to the keeper. Not chasing any wide deliveries outside off.
Much better. Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Beaten! Some movement on this occasion. Steyn dishes out a back of a length ball outside off, shaping away, Karunaratne tries to punch it away but misses due to the excess movement.

Identical to the last delivery. This time Danushka punches it on the up, not exactly timed well but still through the gap at covers. Maharaj is getting a nice cardio session at the moment as once again he chases it down from mid off. Three more runs added to the total.

Fractionally short in length and outside off, Karunaratne punches it off his back foot through covers. A good confident shot, that. It slows down before the rope as the mid off fielder (Maharaj) chases it down. Three runs taken.
Hurls a length delivery in the corridor of uncertainty. It's allowed through to the keeper.
Slips a full ball down the leg side, some movement as it leaves the batsman and beats his attempted flick shot.
Returns to over the wicket and serves it on a length around off. Danushka blocks it from the crease.
Back of a length ball on off, angling in and hurrying up the batsman. Gunathilaka gets an inside edge onto the body as he tries to work it across the line.
Beauty! That's what Philander's aim is from this angle. Bowls it on a length around off and straightens it from there. Gunathilaka ends up pushing and missing inside the line.

FOUR! Gunathilaka takes the off stump guard now rather than middle and leg as Philander switches to 'round the wicket. He sprays a full ball down the leg side and Danushka flicks it uppishly through square leg for a boundary.
Drops it on a length and just around off, it's blocked off the back foot to the off side.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Shortish and outside off, stroked wide of the cover fielder for one.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Digs in a short ball on middle, not much life in this pitch and hence it goes on a good height to the batsman. Gunathilaka turns inside the crease to pull it but finds the fielder in front of square.
Serves it on a length around off, it's defended from the crease to the off side.
Angling away from the batsman outside off, Karunaratne lets it be.
Down to two slips.
Good length ball on middle, defended on the leg side.
Back of a length ball outside off, Dimuth plays it late past the right side of the point fielder and they take a couple again. The outfield is quite slow because of all the rain.

A mishit. Full in length and on middle, Gunathilaka presents a straight bat and it takes the inside edge. Brushes his pads before rolling in front of mid on as they scamper across. Rabada attacks the ball and lets out a throw at the striker's end but no harm done.

Pitches it full and around off, Gunathilaka drives it down the ground, through the legs of his partner at the other end. Maharaj chases it from mid off as the ball slows down on a heavy outfield. A couple taken.
A length ball angling away from the batsman, it's pushed with an open-faced bat to cover-point.
Back of a length delivery on middle, blocked off the back foot to finish the over.
Presses forward and drives it through the line. Finds mid off.

Was there an edge? No appeal made though. Steyn angles across a length ball outside off, a hint of away shape after pitching, Karunaratne has a nervous poke inside the line and misses. There is some noise but the replays show that it's off the bat clipping the front pad.
Bowls it in the zone outside off, it's left alone.
Gets behind the line of the delivery nicely this time and defends it to the leg side.

FOUR! Edgy! It's fuller in length and around off, Karunaratne with a tentative front foot movement tries playing with a straight bat but it takes the outside edge and speeds through slips and gully for a boundary.
Dale Steyn is back and he will operate from the other end.
In the channel outside off, Gunathilaka lets it through to the keeper. End of an eventful first over.

Huge appeal for a caught behind! The umpire though remains still. A delivery down the leg side, Gunathilaka tries to flick but fails to middle it properly. Quinton de Kock collects the ball and lets out a big appeal. The bowler also joins but nothing from the umpire. Faf du Plessis has a chat with Philander and de Kock but none looked entirely convinced and hence no DRS is used. Hello, the replays detect some sound and the Snicko shows a spike. Wow, an early reprieve for Danushka.
Lands it full again and in line of the stumps. Karunaratne gets it away from the inner half of the bat and it rolls through square leg for one. Both the openers are off the mark!
Pitches it full and just around off, Dimuth is on the front foot as he pushes it with an angled bat to cover-point.
This one is angled across the southpaw. Going further away with the seam outside off. Karunaratne allows it through.
Starts with a good length ball on middle. Not enough movement. Gunathilaka works it off his pads through backward square leg and gets off the mark.

All done and it's time to get going. The South African team gets in a quick huddle with Faf du Plessis sharing some words that he forgot to share in the dressing room. Has become a fashion nowadays. Out come the Sri Lankan openers now - Dimuth Karunaratne and Danushka Gunathilaka. Vernon Philander to bowl first up with three slips and a gully. Here we go...
The players are out in the middle with the sun shining now. It's time for the national anthems.

South Africa skipper, Faf du Plessis says the pitch looks dry and will be good for batting. Is banking on the overcast conditions now for early wickets and informs that they are playing three seamers and two spinners. He is satisfied with the preparations and is excited for this game. Admits that winning away from home is the real test and they are looking forward to it.
Sri Lanka skipper, Suranga Lakmal says that they will bat first and informs that Mathews and Herath come in the playing XI. Adds that they are going with three spinners and one fast bowler.
Toss - Suranga Lakmal gets lucky with the coin-toss as Faf du Plessis calls it wrongly. SRI LANKA WILL BAT!

Pitch report - Russel Arnold inspects the playing area. Tells that the groundsmen got very little time to prepare the pitch due to all the rains. Feels that it's a dry pitch with hardly any grass. You win the toss and bat first, reckons the former Sri Lankan spin bowling all-rounder. Also adds that the first day will be the best for batting.
Weather report - It was raining yesterday but it's clear at the moment. The conditions though remain overcast and it could influence the captains' decision at the toss.

The supposedly 'Blockbuster Thursday' is upon us. Time for some Test cricket. Sri Lanka have returned home after getting mixed results in West Indies but will be without their regular skipper Dinesh Chandimal yet again (owing to ball-tampering controversy). Suranga Lakmal will have the command of the side and the hosts will hope he produces the same result as he did in Barbados not too long ago. South Africa, on the other hand, step into the era post AB de Villiers and Morne Morkel, and it's going to be a true challenge for them on the subcontinent pitches. Will their seamers roar? Will their batsmen get tamed by spin? Hello and welcome everyone for the first Test match in Galle and stay with us for all the desired answers.
